articles.title: 'All coming together' - Isak repaying Liverpool faith
articles.summary: Alexander Isak's two goals against Club Brugge take his tally for the season to 10 as the striker continues to show why Liverpool last year paid £125m to bring him to the club.
body: Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.
By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.
Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted £125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.
But Isak is now in a hot streak of form, having scored four goals in his past four games for Liverpool.

articles.title: Poch denied first Man Utd win by Lammens howler at Sporting
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.
body: United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.

Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.

It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought into replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.

Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into back of the net.

articles.title: Isak and Wirtz power Liverpool to easy victory at Club Brugge
articles.summary: Liverpool recovered from their shock defeat to Fenerbahce in their last Champions League outing to beat Club Brugge 3-0 and improve their chances of a top-eight league phase finish.
body: Andoni Iraola's side have had no problem scoring goals in Europe, but faced issues keeping them out. Brugge were most obliging hosts in that respect, a far cry from the regularly free-scoring side that have so far averaged 2.75 goals per game and beaten Inter Milan at the San Siro.

Felix Lemarechal was the home side's greatest threat. But Alexander Isak was far more decisive, netting the opener following Yann Sommer's misplaced pass before rounding off the scoring in the second half with a deft chip to beat the goalkeeper. Sandwiched between was a superb strike from the in-form Florian Wirtz, set up by a surging run from Rio Ngumoha.

Brugge got better, Lemarechal twice forced Alisson into saves and Nicolo Tresoldi, who has scored the same number of Champions League goals as Erling Haaland this term, also called the Brazilian into action. But Liverpool were creatively superior. Momentum is building.

articles.title: Ayer-Shirley Regional High School cancel football game due to ‘contaminated’ equipment
articles.summary: Ayer-Shirley Regional High School has announced that its game against Lunenburg has been canceled after players’ equipment was contaminated. According to Superintendent Dr. Adam Renda, faculty were notified about the issue around 3:30 PM Wednesday afternoon.
body: Despite efforts to replace the equipment, the school was not able to do so in time.

“We feel terrible that we are unable to hold tonight’s game,” The school said in a Facebook post. “Our players have worked hard and were looking forward to taking the field, and we know their families and our community were looking forward to supporting them. We understand how disappointing this news is, especially with such short notice.”

Police have been notified, and an investigation is currently underway. Boston 25 has reached out to both the school and Ayer police for additional details as to what caused the contamination. The school has asked us to reach out to police for details, but we have yet to hear back.
The school will provide updates on the possibility of the game being rescheduled.

articles.title: Burnley break winless home record as Birmingham win at Turf Moor
articles.summary: Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their Sky Bet Championship promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske's strike and Jaydon Banel's own goal.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Birmingham City at Turf Moor on Wednesday night; Clarets make it 24 winless games in a row at home in the league, the longest run in English Football League history.

It is now 24 games since the Clarets last celebrated three points in front of their own fans, a nightmare run that has now stretched to 403 days. It represents the worst sequence in the history of English football.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, remain firmly ensconced in the drop zone. Coach Fabio Celestini has picked up just three points in the five games he has taken charge off since succeeding Nicky Hayen last month and his team were jeered off at the end.

For City, however, it was a timely return to form following the 1-0 defeat at Stoke on Saturday. This was a seventh win in nine for Chris Davies' team and they are just two places and two points off the automatic promotion spots.

articles.title: Week 11 NFL Playoff Bracket: Who’s In, Who’s Out, And Key Tiebreakers
articles.summary: The NFL season has entered its final stretch, and Week 11 tightened the playoff race in both conferences heading into a loaded Thanksgiving week. The Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers both improved to 9-1 and remain the No. 1 seeds in their conferences.
body: The biggest shake-up came on Monday night, when the Washington Commanders beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on a field goal as time expired, snapping Cincinnati's five-game winning streak. In the NFC, the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears are both 8-2 ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit.
Here is the up-to-date NFL Playoff Picture if the playoffs started right now.
The Bills won their sixth straight game with a 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins, and they'll host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

The Denver Broncos also extended their winning streak to six, as rookie Jonah Coleman ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns in a 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Denver and Kansas City are both 8-2, but the Broncos hold the tiebreaker for first place in the AFC West, which leaves the Chiefs as the No. 5 seed despite a 34-7 rout of the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: More Than A Game: Why Ohio State-Michigan Remains College Football's Best Rivalry
articles.summary: From Bo Schembechler to Jim Tressel, Brady Quinn provides a firsthand look at the history, passion and obsession behind college football's greatest rivalry: Ohio State vs. Michigan.
body: "Son, are you ready to go back to Columbus and kick their ass?"

I'll never forget visiting Ann Arbor with my dad and having the opportunity to spend a few moments with the late Michigan head coach, Bo Schembechler. Upon being introduced, Schembechler was told I was from Columbus, Ohio. He shook my hand, looked me dead in the eyes and delivered that line.

My father was floored. He thought it was one of the coolest interactions of my recruitment. Keep in mind, he had two degrees from Ohio State, but he would have signed my letter of intent to play for Michigan that very day had I let him.
That ultimately wasn't my destiny, but the encounter made something abundantly clear: Whether you choose Ohio State or Michigan, you go there to play in "The Game."

articles.title: Depleted PSG attack shows vulnerability in 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma
articles.summary: A 2-2 draw with Roma revealed an attack missing its usual bite, raising questions about whether long-term knee injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have stripped the European champions of their fear factor
body: Have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged? It is too soon to say if injuries have laid low the Champions League's biggest beast, but on the evidence of Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Roma, there might not be quite the same fear factor when opponents find themselves face to face with the kings of Europe's jungle.

Without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball. That was all the more pronounced given that Ousmane Dembele was left on the bench until the penalty with which PSG took a 2-1 lead. Maghnes Akliouche, Senny Mayulu and Ferran Torres are talented forwards, the last good enough to win a World Cup final for Spain. Pair one or even two of them with the potential Ballon d'Or winners who started for PSG in the Champions League final, and the drop-off is not particularly significant.
